title: Protected reference solution: Secure File Transfer
answer: A strong submission for Secure File Transfer starts with a read-only inspection, uses the lesson’s appropriate tool or concept, and reports expected/observed output and exit status. It tests at least one boundary or failure case in a disposable environment and explains distribution/version assumptions. The exact command sequence may differ by system; do not apply state-changing commands to production as part of this exercise.
explanation: The intended objective is to reason about secure file transfer from evidence. Review correctness, safety, reproducibility, and whether the result supports the learner’s conclusion. A contains-all text gate is not an execution test.
review_rubric: Correct concept and appropriate inspection or controlled action.
Expected result, observed evidence, and status are recorded.
Boundary/failure path and compatibility limitations are discussed.
Unsafe side effects are excluded or confined to an isolated, recoverable lab.
